source: ESRI World Imagery via the keyless ArcGIS REST export endpoint
caveat: 0.3-0.5 m resolution shows objects, not nameplates. Cannot certify unit type or measure heights.
what_would_change_this: a recorded judgement on whether the cooling plant is at ground level (where FortyGuard's 2 m field applies) or roof-mounted (where this model does not describe the building at all)

candidates.bbox_order: lon_min, lat_min, lon_max, lat_max (ArcGIS export order)

assessed_by: model (Claude Sonnet 5), single ESRI frame read 2026-08-24, plus a 6x crop of the equipment yard
evidence: 1 source (ESRI World Imagery); no USGS cross-check, so the two-source rule is NOT met
verdict_note: Two linear arrays of regularly-spaced units stand at ground level in a dedicated yard along the long south facade. Enlarged, each unit shows internal fin/coil structure with fan arrays -- characteristic of air-cooled condensers rather than the enclosed radiator-and-stack form generators take. Evidence toward cooling plant, not certification of it. The roof is ridged with no large rooftop array. This is the ground-level condenser-bank geometry the model assumes, on a LONG facade, which is the placement build_standalone_site.py chose from the footprint alone.
limits: Single-source reading at 0. Chillers and generators are not distinguishable at this resolution, so 'ground-level plant' is a statement about WHERE the equipment is, not about what it is. The two-source cross-check is NOT met -- the same weaker standing this project records for Dulles.
